r10-tc1-fix.title: tc1 fix verification
r10-tc1-fix.imperative: Independently recompute the order-control paragraph's numbers from the Results table and confirm the paragraph's claims and supporting arithmetic are both correct and mutually consistent -- not just that the words 'and magnitude' were removed.
r10-tc1-fix.finding: The LITERAL tc1 defect from attempt-2 (claiming orders 'agree in direction and magnitude') is gone -- the text now says 'agree in direction' only and explicitly says 'They do not agree in magnitude'. But the arithmetic newly cited to support that claim is the WRONG quantity and is internally inconsistent with the claim it is attached to. Recomputed independently from the published Results table (rep1-cli=21, rep2-cli=23, rep1-mcp=19, rep2-mcp=17): the paragraph now cites 'the CLI arm's attempts differ by 2 between orders (21 vs 23) and the MCP arm's by 2 (19 vs 17)' -- this is each ARM's own across-order spread (a within-arm quantity), and both spreads are IDENTICAL (2 and 2), which if anything reads as agreement, not disagreement -- it does not logically support 'they do not agree in magnitude' at all. The quantity that DOES support that claim, and that motivated the original tc1 finding (attempt-2 review: '+2 vs +6, a 3x difference'), is the per-order CLI-vs-MCP GAP: order 'CLI first' shows a gap of 21-19=2, order 'MCP first' shows a gap of 23-17=6 -- a 3x difference. That 2-vs-6 figure is nowhere in the v3 text; it has been replaced by a different, non-supporting pair of numbers. Net effect: the paragraph's own math no longer demonstrates the magnitude-instability it claims to demonstrate, and the real, sharper instability (2 vs 6, bearing directly on how much the n=2 headline gap can be trusted) has quietly disappeared from the document -- which is exactly the kind of caveat-softening-under-review-pressure the Commander asked me to check for in concern 4, even though it wasn't the mechanism I expected going in. One-line fix: restate the paragraph using the per-order CLI-MCP gap (2 vs 6) rather than the within-arm order-to-order spread.
